title: A Wall Card That Explains an Idea Before It Asks | vitalii.no
description:
How a homework kiosk stopped matching questions to templates and started teaching the idea behind them first, with every animation traceable to a real source.

A wall card used to be built bottom-up: my son made a math question, a template matched the shape of that question, and the kiosk printed it. That draws a tidy exercise but never explains the idea underneath it. A child who doesn't know that 25% is a quarter learns nothing from watching a quarter of a bar get shaded next to the answer.

A new layer sits above the templates. A card now resolves to a didactic model — the actual method real teaching uses to make one idea visible, paired with the misconception it exists against and a verbatim source that backs it up. Each model plays as five beats: the idea appears, the movement runs, one worked case is shown, then the card asks and withholds the answer. AI research agents do the literature research and storyboard work, and a verification script is the gate: it fails any sourced claim that has no quote attached, because an animation nobody actually uses is worse than having none.

The wall now teaches nine verified pedagogical models instead of matching a template to the shape of a question, each one traceable to a real source rather than an invented explanation.
